title: Relay failover trigger taxonomy and circuit-safety policy for regional/tier routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We currently rely on ad-hoc thresholds in multiple services to trigger model variant fallbacks and region soft-failovers. That has led to inconsistent behavior across tiers: e.g., a burst of 429s in a single AZ produced immediate eviction for some tenants but only RT timeouts for others. We need a unified taxonomy of 'fail signals' and a deterministic policy engine that converts those signals into safe, observable actions (soft-degrade, model-variant fallback, regional reroute) with clear hysteresis and probation windows.

Goal: Deliver a canonical taxonomy of failure triggers (429 surge, request-level timeout, backend timeout, sustained error-rate, per-tenant throttling), map each to a prioritized action set per routing tier (hot, warm, cold), and produce a circuit-safety policy that includes trip thresholds, decay/probation rules, and mitigation rollbacks. The policy must be implementable by the Smart Routing controller and plumbed into the Console rollout UI and Alerting/Telemetry pipelines.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Taxonomy doc published and reviewed by SRE, Serving, and PM.
2) Policy engine specification (finite-state trip model) with hysteresis and decay rules merged in the spec PR.
3) A prototype implementation in the routing controller that can be toggled via feature-flag, with unit-tests covering trip/open/half-open/close transitions.
4) End-to-end integration test that simulates 429 spikes, backend timeouts, and increasing error-rate and demonstrates expected actions (soft-degrade -> variant-fallback -> regional-cutover) in order.
5) Telemetry queries & Grafana dashboard created showing trip scores, per-tenant probation state, and rollback events.
6) Runbook entries and postmortem template updated to reference the new taxonomy.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (spec + reviews, 2w): publish taxonomy and policy model; gather sign-offs from SRE and Product.
Phase 2 (canary implementation, 3w): implement policy in router with feature-flag; run limited canary on internal tenants; collect telem.
Phase 3 (observability + runbook, 1w): dashboards, alerts, and runbook.
Phase 4 (gradual ramp, 2w): enable for 10% of production traffic, then 50%, then 100% with rollback gates at each stage.
Post-rollout: 2-week watch with oncall and ENG owners assigned.
Rollback criteria: unexpected increase in end-to-end 95th latency, or >2% increase in user-facing error-rate attributable to routing changes.
telemetry:
We will emit:
- relay.trip_score (gauge) per tenant, region, tier
- relay.trip_state (enum) OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED per tenant
- relay.trigger_reason (tagged: 429, timeout, error_rate, backend_fail)
- relay.action_taken (soft_degrade, variant_fallback, region_reroute)
Alerting: Page if >5 tenants enter OPEN state in a region within 5m or if a single tenant flips to OPEN more than 3x in 15m. Dashboards: per-tenant probation timelines, cohort heatmap by region/tier, and SRV-level correlation with model-variant metrics (latency/cost/quality).
notes:
Implementation details considered during design review: prefer a decoupled trip calculator service (stateless scoring with sliding-window counters) vs an in-router local state machine. Tradeoffs: central calculator simplifies consistent decisions but adds latency and a single point of failure; local scoring reduces cross-service calls but risks divergence. Proposal: local scoring with periodic reconciliation to a leader-backed truth store.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical window for error-rate and 95th latency measurement? Initial proposal: 1m/5m/1h buckets for short-term, mid-term, and long-term signals.
- How to express tenant-specific SLOs and exempt critical customers from automatic regional reroute? Plan: per-tenant policy overrides stored in config service.
- Where should cost-aware fallbacks live (prefer cheaper quantized variants) vs quality-preserving fallbacks? We'll add a priority vector to action mappings.
